assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defines the physiology of the incretin hormone GLP-1 (proglucagon processing, insulinotropic action, appetite and gastric effects) and led to therapies that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity treatment. Originality, clarity and very large clinical and societal impact are all strong.
assessment.attribution: The credited set has four names. Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (mechanism and therapeutic proof of concept) and Mojsov (peptide identification and synthesis) best represent the discovery arc; Knudsen's contribution is more drug-development oriented. Credit among Mojsov and other early contributors not on the list is historically contested, and I have not independently verified details.
assessment.maturity: Therapeutic confirmation is overwhelming and multiply replicated in large outcome trials. Timing is highly appropriate given the global use of the drugs.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among the early GLP-1 peptide characterisation groups is disputed.
The list omits some contributors (e.g. pioneering proglucagon sequencing groups), which may complicate a fair three-person configuration.
Whether drug development (Knudsen) should count versus physiology is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells redirected to tumour antigens produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new therapeutic modality (living drugs). The conceptual step, from chimeric receptor design to costimulation to clinical proof, is original and has lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (costimulated CAR design, 19-28z) and June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T with 4-1BB) are decisive; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and TIL and early gene-engineered T cells, so credit is plausible but the CAR design itself is not his. The supplied credit supports a three-person prize, though Rosenberg's inclusion depends on how the committee frames the discovery.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products, long-term follow-up of survivors with persistent remissions in some patients and replicated trials. Solid-tumour efficacy and toxicity remain limits, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Whether Rosenberg's cell-therapy work or Eshhar's early chimeric receptors (not on the list) should be recognised.
Long-term safety, including secondary T-cell malignancies, is still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-gated ion channels from algae, expressed in neurons, gave causal control of defined cell populations with millisecond precision and transformed neuroscience and studies of circuits and behaviour. Very high originality and broad lasting methodological impact across fields.
assessment.attribution: Six credited names. Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) identified and characterised channelrhodopsin; Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated neuronal application; Miesenboeck's earlier genetically targeted photoactivation is also decisive. Only three can be selected and the choice cuts out strong contributors, which is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated for nearly two decades and routine in laboratories; clinical translation for vision restoration is emerging. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Allocation among Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck versus the three selected is unresolved.
The medical rather than tool impact is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response as a novel organelle-to-nucleus signalling pathway (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing) establishing how cells monitor ER protein-folding capacity. Conceptually original, clean mechanistic work with broad relevance to secretory disease, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the clearly decisive pair, with Walter defining IRE1 and the unconventional splicing mechanism and Mori the cis element and signalling pathway. The two-person configuration is clean.
assessment.maturity: Findings are extensively confirmed and textbook. Recognition by the Lasker award suggests maturity, and a prize would be timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Therapeutic translation (e.g. ISRIB, IRE1 inhibitors) remains early.
Overlap with other proteostasis and ER stress contributors outside the list is not assessed here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) is a rare case of a mechanistic RNA-biology discovery producing a disease-modifying therapy for a previously lethal childhood disease. Strong clarity and clinical impact, and it validated antisense therapeutics broadly.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism, ISS-N1 target) and Bennett (oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development) are the natural pair. Others, such as Hua and Singh, contributed to the target discovery and are not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with several years of real-world and trial confirmation, including in presymptomatic infants. Long-term durability data are still accumulating.
uncertainties: Role of other contributors in target identification complicates attribution.
Platform breadth versus a single-drug story is a question of framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids from Lgr5+ cells established long-term culture of self-organising epithelial tissue and opened new models for development, disease, host-microbe study and personalised medicine. The underlying Lgr5 stem-cell discovery was also important.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is clearly the lead and Sato was first author of the key intestinal organoid paper. The pair is fair, though Clevers may be viewed as the principal figure.
assessment.maturity: Technique widely replicated and adopted, but clinical impact (drug screening, transplantation) is still emerging and some claims are early.
uncertainties: Clinical translation is not yet demonstrated at scale.
Overlap with other organoid and pluripotent-stem-cell organoid contributions (e.g. Sasai, Lancaster, Knoblich) is not on the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers, with real-world population effects showing substantial decline in disease. Important, original and with large public-health impact.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller's L1 VLP work and Frazer's parallel VLP development, along with others not on the list (e.g. Zhou, Kirnbauer), make a fair three-person prize possible, but priority issues exist. Zur Hausen's earlier prize covers the virus-cancer link.
assessment.maturity: Efficacy and population-level reductions in HPV infection and CIN are strongly confirmed, with cancer reduction data now emerging. The timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Priority among Frazer, Zhou and the NCI team is a contested allocation.
Overlap with the previous 2008 prize may weigh against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chaperonin-assisted protein folding, from the discovery of mitochondrial Hsp60 function to the GroEL/GroES cycle, showed that folding is actively assisted in the cell. Original and general, with relevance to protein-misfolding disease.
assessment.attribution: Hartl and Horwich are a coherent and long-standing pair; Lasker-recognised. Other chaperone pioneers (e.g. Ellis) lie outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well established and mature, though possibly seen as classic biochemistry with less direct medical impact than other candidates.
uncertainties: Neighbouring chaperone credit (e.g. Ellis, Georgopoulos) is not supplied.
